cf.title: Fix jsonpath printing of operations followed by an accessor

input.subject: Fix jsonpath printing of operations followed by an accessor

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The first message states the bug with reproducible examples: a printed jsonpath that returns a different result or does not parse, which reaches users through pg_dump and pg_get_viewdef(). The fix extends the rule printJsonPathItem() already uses for numeric literals. Confidence is medium because only one message is visible and the code was not read.

brief.title: Fix jsonpath output dropping parentheses before an accessor
brief.problem: The jsonpath output function drops parentheses around an operation followed by an accessor or method, so the printed path means something else or does not parse. Because pg_dump and pg_get_viewdef() use this output, a view can return different results after dump and restore, and a jsonpath column can fail to restore. The bug dates from v12.
brief.proposed_design: printJsonPathItem() decides about parentheses only from operator priority. The patch makes it parenthesize any operation or predicate that has an accessor after it, the same way it already handles numeric literals. Regression tests print each kind and compare query results before and after a reparse.
user_visible_surface: jsonpath output text changes for paths whose printed form is wrong today, which also changes pg_dump output and view, rule and index definitions.
author_claims: '(-$.a).abs() + 1' on {"a": -2} returns 3, but its printed form returns -1.
On v15 and later some printed forms, such as '($.a + 1).abs() == 2', fail with "trailing junk after numeric literal".
"!", "is unknown" and "exists" followed by an accessor print in a form that fails to parse on every version tried.
Output changes only for paths that print wrong today.
A fuzzer found only this bug on master and found no mismatch in three runs of 20,000 expressions with the patch.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible. The author offers versions for REL_14 to REL_16 if a back-patch is wanted.
unclear: The patch does not say how existing dumps that hold the broken printed forms should be handled on restore.
The author does not say whether the fuzzer is available or what grammar subset it covers.
The thread does not say how stored views, rules and indexes built from the old output are affected after a minor upgrade.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: pg_dump and pg_get_viewdef() emit jsonpath output text, which the patch changes for paths that print wrong today.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The bug dates from v12, and the author offers versions for REL_14 to REL_16 if a back-patch is wanted.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Does every printed form that the patch changes still parse, with the same meaning, on each supported older release that might load a newer dump?
What should users do with dumps already taken that hold the broken printed forms, and does that belong in the release notes?
If the fix is back-patched, can any index or stored value built on jsonpath text output differ after the minor upgrade?
Which parts of the jsonpath grammar does the fuzzer generate, and can you post it so reviewers can repeat the runs?
Does a jsonpath operator or predicate added later get parentheses under the new rule without a further change to printJsonPathItem()?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the jsonpath parser and output code in jsonpath.c, and who can judge a back-patch that changes output text.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the changed jsonpath output text on every branch that gets the fix, including dump and restore across minor versions, for as long as those branches are supported.
committability.author_follow_up: The author offers to send versions for REL_14 to REL_16 if the fix is back-patched; no other sign yet.

priority.reason: The bug gives wrong results and failed restores, but only for paths with a parenthesized operation followed by an accessor. The patch is 8.8 KiB, touches jsonpath.c and its regression test, and adds no new user-visible surface.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the claim that output changes only for paths that print wrong today is unchecked. Whether the new rule covers every operation and predicate kind is also unchecked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add jsonpath string method $.replace(from, to)
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andrew Dunstan, "David E(dot) Wheeler", Peter Eisentraut
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a non-standard jsonpath string method, $.replace(from, to), which calls the internal implementation of the SQL replace() function on a JSON string value. The author planned more text methods, such as trim(), upper() and lower().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread does not state why the author withdrew the entry. David E. Wheeler noted that replace() is not in the SQL/JSON spec, and Andrew Dunstan objected that a future spec version could add an incompatible method with the same name, so he wanted non-spec method names prefixed or capitalized. Peter Eisentraut asked for a general way to call any suitable pg_proc function from jsonpath, and the author then began sketching that design instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The thing that bothers me about the original proposal
is this: what if we add a new non-spec jsonpath method and then a new
version of the spec adds a method with the same name, but not compatible
with our method?

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow subfield references without parentheses
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets column references with three or more identifiers be read as a correlation name, a column and one or more composite-type fields, as the SQL standard allows, so `A.B.C` can mean `(A.B).C`. The correlation must be an explicit alias, and the parser raises an error when both readings apply.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Tom Lane raised possible new ambiguity but agreed with raising an error, and Ashutosh Bapat suggested building the reference through transformIndirection(). The patch also still had TODOs for documentation and for SQL and PL/pgSQL parameters, and no reply after 2024-12-13 is shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: tab-completion debug print
precedents_retrieved.summary: Instrument psql's tab-complete.c so that each completion prints the source line number that produced it, and later the completion text, to stderr. The first version was a compile-time option (TABCOMPLETION_DEBUG); a later version made it a run-time psql option, -g.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut and Tom Lane objected to the run-time option. They said it should not use a short option letter, and that it is a development aid that should stay out of production builds. Peter Eisentraut also asked for evidence of tab completion problems in production that would need it. Michael Paquier closed it as returned with feedback, citing a suggestion of Tom's from a message not shown here.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This is a development option,
not a production option.  I don't think it should be in production
builds at all, let alone be invokable via a simple command-line switch.

precedents_retrieved.title: Dump-restore loosing 'attnotnull' bit for DEFERRABLE PRIMARY KEY column(s)
precedents_retrieved.summary: A bug report: after dump and restore, a column covered only by a DEFERRABLE PRIMARY KEY loses attnotnull, because pg_dump emits a throwaway NOT NULL constraint and then drops it. The author's patch changes pg_dump to skip the throwaway NOT NULL constraint for deferrable primary keys.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Before the patch was posted, Alvaro Herrera said the more critical fix was in the backend, which should reject the DROP CONSTRAINT, and that ATExecDropNotNull() should stop relying on RelationGetIndexAttrBitmap. No message after the patch shows a review or a decision.

precedents_retrieved.title: Removing unused trailing linepointers from heap pages
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch truncates unused line pointers at the end of a heap page's line pointer array, which lowers pd_lower and returns that space for tuple data. Later versions also did this truncation during pruning, beyond the VACUUM-only truncation added in Postgres 14.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Geoghegan asked for concrete evidence before the patch could be committed: a benchmark or test showing a measurable benefit, such as smaller on-disk table size, or at least no regressions. That request went unanswered and the thread stalled, so the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I just want to see
some concrete testing, maybe with pgbench, or with an artificial test
case.

precedents_retrieved.title: Avoid computing ORDER BY junk columns unnecessarily
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a projection at the end of grouping_planner() that removes junk columns added only for ORDER BY or GROUP BY, so expensive sort expressions satisfied by an index are not computed. To mark which junk columns can be removed, it turns the resjunk boolean into an enum.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane found that the patch changes only the final top-level targetlist, so lower plan nodes still compute the expensive expression and cost estimates do not reflect the saving. He also thought the resjunk enum change was invasive and suggested waiting for the work on unifying index scans and index-only scans. Richard Guo found Assert failures with postgres_fdw and with FOR UPDATE queries, and CFbot later reported test failures with no new version posted.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: My basic complaint is that this is a band-aid that only touches things at a surface level, whereas I think we need a much deeper set of changes in order to have a plausible solution.

precedents_retrieved.title: doc: a restore executes code chosen by any dumped object's owner
precedents_retrieved.summary: A documentation patch widens the dump/restore warning added by 71ea0d6795 in pg_dump, pg_dumpall and pg_restore, so it covers code chosen by any owner of a dumped object instead of only source superusers. It adds two examples: a CHECK constraint and a stored generated column, both evaluated during COPY with the privileges of the role that runs the restore.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The thread has only the author's first message, with no replies, and the entry was later marked withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.title: Use JOIN USING aliases in ruleutils.c
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes ruleutils.c so that, when JOIN USING output columns conflict with other names in a query, it attaches generated JOIN USING aliases (a feature added in Postgres 14) and qualifies the columns with them. This replaces the old approach of renaming those columns to be unique across the whole query.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the new output would reduce pg_dump portability, since dumped views would no longer load into pre-v14 servers or other database systems. He also saw little gain: the patch added code to ruleutils.c on net, and the regression test output was not clearly better. The author agreed and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
My big fear is that it will reduce portability of pg_dump output:
views that would have loaded successfully into pre-v14 servers
no longer will, and your chances of porting them to other RDBMSes
probably go down too.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert cascading of JSON_TABLE's ON ERROR
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert cascading of JSON_TABLE's ON ERROR
Reverted commit(s): JSON_TABLE PLAN clause
precedents_retrieved.objection:
86ab7f4c721d commit made the table-level ON ERROR clause serve as the default
ON ERROR for columns lacking their own, so that a top-level ERROR ON ERROR
turned per-column evaluation errors into hard errors.

The SQL standard does mandate this cascade, but introducing it should be
a deliberate, separately-documented change, so restore the previous
behavior for now.  This also reverts the paired ruleutils.c logic that
deparsed a column's behavior against an ERROR default: that dropped an
explicit ERROR ON EMPTY from a dumped view, and otherwise emitted a
redundant NULL ON EMPTY.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert support for improved tracking of nested queries
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert support for improved tracking of nested queries
Reverted commit(s): Track more precisely query locations for nested statements; Fix regression with location calculation of nested statements; pg_stat_statements: Add tests for nested queries with level tracking
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This commit reverts the two following commits:
- 499edb09741b, track more precisely query locations for nested
statements.
- 06450c7b8c70, a follow-up fix of 499edb09741b with query locations.
The test introduced in this commit is not reverted.  This is proving
useful to track a problem that only pgaudit was able to detect.

These prove to have issues with the tracking of SELECT statements, when
these use multiple parenthesis which is something supported by the
grammar.  Incorrect location and lengths are causing pg_stat_statements
to become confused, failing its job in query normalization with
potential out-of-bound writes because the location and the length may
not match with what can be handled.  A lot of the query patterns
discussed when this issue was reported have no test coverage in the main
regression test suite, or the recovery test 027_stream_regress.pl would
have caught the problems as pg_stat_statements is loaded by the node
running the regression tests.  A first step would be to improve the test
coverage to stress more the query normalization logic.

A different portion of this work was done in 45e0ba30fc40, with the
addition of tests for nested queries.  These can be left in the tree.
They are useful to track the way inner queries are currently tracked by
PGSS with non-top-level entries, and will be useful when reconsidering
in the future the work reverted here.

precedents_retrieved.title: A COLLATE clause in the URI of XMLNAMESPACES does not read back
precedents_retrieved.summary:
A COLLATE clause in the URI of XMLNAMESPACES does not read back
Threads: [DEPARSE] A COLLATE clause in the URI of XMLNAMESPACES does not read back

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. P24 is a different deparse bug in XMLNAMESPACES with no recorded reason. P13 reverts a JSON_TABLE behaviour change, and its reason (an unannounced semantic change) does not apply to a bug fix in jsonpath output, so neither carries a reason that applies here.

This is a deparse bug fix. The new output is the only form that reads back with the same meaning, and the text changes only for paths that print wrongly today, so I found no compatibility objection worth sending. Not checkable without the code: whether every changed form still parses on older servers, which matters when a new dump is loaded into an older release. A committer would also likely weigh, for a back-patch, that dumps already taken with the broken forms stay wrong, and that indexes built on jsonpath text output would change.

The patch changes only the jsonpath output text; the binary jsonpath format in heap columns and stored view, rule and index expressions stays the same, so pg_upgrade and existing data are unaffected. Dumps and logical replication text taken from unfixed servers keep the old broken forms, but that is the existing bug, which the patch does not make worse.

The patch changes only how the jsonpath output function prints parentheses, and adds no privilege, role, function or exposure path. The existing bug could change the meaning of a jsonpath in an RLS policy or security barrier view after dump and restore, but that argues for the fix.

From the maintenance angle this is a narrow bug fix in printJsonPathItem() that follows the existing numeric-literal rule. It adds no hot-path cost, no new API and no lasting commitment, and its tests compare results after a reparse. Without the code, I could not check whether future jsonpath operators fall under the new rule without any extra change.

This is a bug fix to the jsonpath output function. No existing feature, setting or extension gives a correct printed form, so users cannot avoid the broken pg_dump and view-definition output today. Whether the fix fits in core needs no answer, and the patch extends the existing parenthesization logic for numeric literals.

This is a correctness bug fix: jsonpath output that changes query results or fails to restore through pg_dump affects anyone who uses such paths, and no workaround exists for dump round-trips. Demand is not the test for a wrong-result and failed-restore bug, and the output change is limited to paths that print wrong today.
